event: Weekly Market Review
title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Semis melted up, then unwound Friday; energy and defensives absorbed it.
SOXX ran +9.35% on the week before a -3.67% Friday shellacking knocked QQQ below its 200-day. Energy led all sectors and gold/silver were dumped, so the arc was a chip-led melt-up that cracked rather than a broad risk-on. Large beat small by 1.46pp.

INDICES — QQQ +3.63%, SPY +2.59%, RSP +2.37%, IWM +1.41%, DIA +2.13%. Large caps outgained small (large +3.63% vs small +2.17%). VIX closed 19.3, above its 19.4 20-day average and elevated in the 13.5–31.1 band. Gold was the week's biggest cross-asset move at -4.58% (GLD), with silver -5.85% and the dollar up 2.01% over 20 days. QQQ is the only major index below its 200-day MA.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLE Energy +5.42%, XLI Industrials +3.76%, XLC Comm Services +3.72%, XLK Tech +3.36%, XLF Financials +2.66%, XLP Staples +2.52%, XLV Health Care +2.19%, XLU Utilities +2.11%, XLY Discretionary +2.04%, XLRE Real Estate +0.84%, XLB Materials +0.54%. Industries: SOXX +9.35% and UNG +8.56% led; MSOS -12.26% and IBIT -9.19% lagged. Money went into SOXX (+$25.4bn, 100th pct), QQQ (+$6.2bn) and RSP (+$2.3bn) while SPY bled -$4.4bn and XLF -$919m. Label: AI hardware fading / high-to-low rotation.

DRIVERS — The chip complex was the whole story: SOXX +9.35% led everything but reversed -3.67% Friday, with AMD -8.75% and AVGO -4.76% on the day and QQQ -1.20%. Semis' collapse dragged Nasdaq into a -1.20% Friday while DIA held green +0.13% and XLP +1.42%, XLC +1.05% and XLE +0.98% absorbed flows — the classic high-to-low handoff. Outside equities, GLD -4.58% and SLV -5.85% fell hard as the dollar firmed (UUP +2.01% 20d); oil was soft on the week with USO -10.00% over 20 days despite crude stocks building +465.7 vs -110.9 forecast. Breadth stayed constructive underneath: 314 advancers, 71% above 50DMA, but up/down volume was 0.81.

WHAT'S NEXT — QQQ sitting under its 200-day with VXN at 29.4 (above 28.1 ma20) and QQQ ATM IV 24.9% is the risk pivot: either it reclaims the line or the semiconductor unwind extends. Retail Sales, Industrial Production and Housing Starts print Nov 17–18 with forecast 0 and +0.10 respectively, a genuine macro test after PPI came in hot at 6.5% y/y. And watch energy: XLE led at +5.42% but is still -4.81% over 20 days — the sector's first real inflection in a month.
